subject: On-prem connectivity: asymmetrical routing, NAT and MTU causing inference timeouts
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-logistics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2025 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Degraded connectivity to Redwood Private nodes after router changes

Hannah,

We noticed a sharp increase in inference timeouts and TCP retransmits to the Redwood Private cluster after a network change this morning. The symptoms: intermittent packet loss at ~0.5-1%, frequent TCP retransmits, and some requests failing with early connection resets.

Attached a small packet capture and a brief traceroute output. From our perspective the failures started after we applied the new route policy and enabled NAT on the east-edge-router. Traceroute shows asymmetric paths for return traffic.

Can you triage with your engs? Happy to jump on a call — we can provide router logs and full pcaps.

Attachments: packet_capture_initial.pcap (200KB), traceroute.txt

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Logistics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2025 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Degraded connectivity to Redwood Private nodes after router changes

Thanks for the heads up, Lena — sorry you hit this. I've looped in Marcus (network SE) and Grace (SRE) to lead the debugging. Quick asks to help prioritize:

- Can you paste the edge router's route table and NAT translation summary (show running-config / ip nat translations)?
- Can you confirm if DF (Don't Fragment) is set on hosts or if MTU was changed on the new policy?
- Do you have the exact time window when you flipped the policy?

Marcus / Grace — initial hypothesis: asymmetric routing and NAT change could be causing path MTU issues or asymmetric source IPs leading to stateful firewall drops. Marcus, please propose a minimal test (MSS clamp, temporary SNAT disable on a small subnet, or targeted packet mirror).

We should keep this scoped and avoid broad failovers until we understand impact; Lena — will you allow us to run a short (5–10m) test that modifies NAT behavior for one host?

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2025 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Degraded connectivity to Redwood Private nodes after router changes

Quick notes from my initial review of the pcap and traceroute:

- I see a lot of TCP segments with the DF bit set and ICMP "fragmentation needed" responses that never reach the sender (likely dropped by an intermediate device).
- The path shows return traffic coming back via a different transit that has MTU 1500; the origin subnet is doing 9000 on the iSCSI/transit segment — potential MTU mismatch.
- NAT summary (from provided logs) indicates an additional SNAT translation applied at the east-edge, which would change the source IP seen by one of our stateful firewalls; if return path uses a different NAT device, connections could be asymmetrically translated leading to drops.

Suggested immediate mitigations (low risk):
1) Apply MSS clamping on the east-edge-router for TCP flows from the affected subnet (reduces need for fragmentation).
2) Temporarily disable the new SNAT rule for a small test prefix and monitor (10 hosts).
3) Verify security-group / firewall stateful rules allow traffic from both pre- and post-NAT source IP ranges; add a temporary rule if necessary.

I've attached a short router config snippet I want you to confirm: router-config.txt. Lena — can you run the following (or grant access for a 10m window)?

- show ip nat translations | include <affected-subnet>
- show route table
- show interface | include MTU

I'll stand by for your outputs — we can do a quick call if you prefer.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
NetEng, Redwood Inference

From: SRE Team <sre@acme-logistics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Degraded connectivity to Redwood Private nodes after router changes

Marcus / Hannah — thanks. We've pulled the configs and confirmed two issues:

1) The east-edge-router was configured with SNAT for the tenant subnet during the deploy (intent was outbound NAT for vendor peering). The downstream transit uses a different NAT gateway for the return path, so state is not present on the original translation device.

2) MTU mismatch: our internal SAN/transit had jumbo frames (9000) and the new transit path has 1500. Because DF is set on the app hosts we see ICMP "fragmentation needed" but the intermediate transit is dropping ICMP due to security policy.

Actions we're taking now:
- Enabling MSS clamping on the east-edge-router (in progress).
- Adding temporary firewall rules to allow ICMP "frag needed" between the two transit hops (will be reverted after verification).
- Rolling back the SNAT rule for a single test prefix (we'll provide the prefix in a follow-up).

We expect measurable improvement within the next 30–45 minutes; however, the cluster may still see some slow tails until all TCP sessions refresh.

-- SRE Team (Acme)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: SRE Team <sre@acme-logistics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Degraded connectivity to Redwood Private nodes after router changes

Appreciate the quick turnaround, team. Marcus / Grace — we need to coordinate a controlled failover window for the Dedicated inference shard serving Acme. Lena — thanks for the temporary changes; from Redwood's side we'll: 

- Run a canary failover (redirect ~5% traffic) to an alternate shard to validate that connectivity remains stable under real traffic.
- Hold on any cluster restarts until after the canary; we'll only escalate to a full failover if the canary shows no improvement.

Proposed window: Wed 2025-11-13 11:30–11:45 PST. Lena — confirm; if that works I'll trigger the canary and share monitoring links.

Checklist for the window (internal):
- Marcus: confirm MSS clamp is applied and NAT rollback for test prefix is in place.
- Grace: prepare rollback runbook and monitoring dashboards (latency, 5xx, retransmits).
- Jonas: notify CS + account manager and prepare customer comms if we need extended actions.

Jonas — can you draft a 1–2 line notification for the account if the canary goes to full failover?

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-logistics.com>, SRE Team <sre@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Postmortem: MTU/NAT mismatch - resolved and next steps

Summary: The outage was caused by two interacting config changes at Acme: an unintended SNAT on the east-edge path and a MTU mismatch (9000 vs 1500) with intermediate ICMP filtered. These together caused asymmetric connectivity and prevented PMTUD, leading to TCP fragmentation failures and increased retransmits.

What we did:
- Acme enabled MSS clamping and allowed ICMP "fragmentation needed" between transit hops.
- They rolled back the SNAT for the affected test prefix; we validated session establishment from that prefix.
- Redwood ran a 15-minute canary failover and observed normal p95 latency and no new 5xx errors.

Impact: 10–15 minutes of elevated tail latency for a small subset of requests during the initial deploy and an additional 30–45 minutes while TCP sessions cycled. No data loss observed.

Action items (owners):
- Acme: update change runbook to flag MTU harmonization checks before edge deployments (Lena).
- Redwood / Marcus: add automated MSS clamp recommendation to our private deployment preflight check (INF-4512).
- Redwood / Grace: add a monitoring alert for asymmetric route flaps and high ICMP frag-needed counts (alert playbook in runbook link).

Attachments: postmortem-20251114.pdf (runbook excerpt), edge-route-table.txt, router-config.txt

Thanks everyone for the fast collaboration — happy to schedule a short retro next week to tighten the deploy checklist.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
